extracted_concepts.name: Sample Space
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Set Ω of all possible outcomes of a random experiment.

extracted_concepts.name: Classical Probability Model
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: P(A)=|A|/|Ω| when outcomes are equally likely.

extracted_concepts.name: Bayes' Theorem
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Updates P(A_j|B) using prior probabilities and likelihoods.

extracted_concepts.name: Binomial Distribution
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Distribution B(n,p) of number of successes.

extracted_concepts.name: Poisson Distribution
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Discrete distribution P(λ) for rare-event counts.

extracted_concepts.name: Transformation of Random Variable
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Find distribution of Y=g(X) via CDF or transformation formula.

extracted_concepts.name: Marginal Distribution
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Obtain f_X or f_Y by integrating the joint density.

extracted_concepts.name: Chi-square Distribution
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Distribution used for normal variance inference.

extracted_concepts.name: t Distribution
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Distribution used when σ is unknown.

extracted_concepts.name: Method of Moments
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Estimate parameters by equating sample and population moments.

extracted_concepts.name: Consistency
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: θ̂ converges in probability to θ.

extracted_concepts.name: Confidence Interval
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Interval estimate such as X̄ ± margin.

extracted_concepts.name: Hypothesis Testing
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Decide between H₀ and H₁ using a test statistic.

extracted_concepts.name: Z-test
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Test for mean with known σ.

extracted_concepts.name: t-test
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Test for mean with unknown σ.

extracted_relations.evidence: Defined from probabilities P(AB) and P(A).
Independence is often interpreted through P(B|A)=P(B).
Joint distribution describes X and Y.
Marginals are obtained from joint density.
E(X) is computed from distribution of X.
X̄ is computed from observations of X.
Test statistic T follows t distribution under H₀.
Z-test is a normal-mean hypothesis test.
Likelihood is product of densities f(x_i;θ).
